description: Fully autonomous & self-evolving research from idea to paper. Chat an Idea. Get a Paper. 🦞

summary.one_liner: AutoResearchClaw is a Python pipeline that turns a single research topic into a full academic paper, with literature search, sandbox experiments, peer review, and LaTeX export, running fully autonomously or with human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
summary.what_it_does: The pipeline runs 23 stages across 8 phases: scoping, literature discovery from OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and arXiv, knowledge synthesis, hypothesis generation, experiment design and code generation, sandboxed execution with self-repair, result analysis with a PROCEED/REFINE/PIVOT decision, paper drafting, multi-agent peer review, and export to NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR LaTeX templates. Outputs include paper_draft.md, paper.tex, references.bib, a citation verification report, experiment code and metrics, charts, and reviews. Citations are checked through arXiv, CrossRef/DataCite, Semantic Scholar and LLM relevance scoring. A HITL Co-Pilot system offers six intervention modes, and an opt-in MetaClaw bridge carries lessons from past runs into later ones. Version 0.5.0 adds domain-specific experiment agents for high-energy physics, biology and statistics, plus the ARC-Bench benchmark of 55 research topics.
use_cases: Generate a draft academic paper from a research idea
Automate literature review with real citations
Run sandboxed ML experiments and collect metrics automatically
Co-pilot a paper with human review at key decision points
Verify that references in a paper are real and relevant
Produce conference-formatted LaTeX from a research topic
Run physics or biology research pipelines with domain-specific agents
notable: 23-stage autonomous pipeline with self-healing experiment repair and PIVOT/REFINE decision loop
4-layer citation verification that removes hallucinated references
Six HITL intervention modes including co-pilot, step-by-step and gate-only
Works through any ACP-compatible coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and others) without a separate API key
Domain-specialist experiment agents for high-energy physics, biology and statistics, plus the ARC-Bench benchmark
caveats: Experiments run in a sandbox or Docker and depend on local hardware; GPU/MPS/CPU support is auto-detected
Requires an LLM API key or a supported agent CLI, and LaTeX compilation needs a separate LaTeX install
Optional features such as the physics pipeline need extra external tools (MadGraph5, FeynRules, Delphes via a cloud service); MetaClaw and OpenClaw integrations are opt-in
The README describes the project as being in testing, and the pipeline is still being refined based on tester feedback
